signal: A regulation with a deadline applies to the segment
fresh_window: From announcement to the deadline; strongest 3 to 12 months before it
what_it_means: Every company in scope must change a process, document something or buy a tool by a fixed date. Many start late.
good_for_sellers_of: Compliance and security software, finance and HR tools, consultancies
find_with_clay: Company search by the industries, sizes and countries the rule covers. Then a Custom data point: 'Does this company say publicly that it is preparing for [regulation]? Quote the source.'
find_without_clay: The regulator's scope definition, industry association pages, news. Ask your AI who is in scope and by when.
message_angle: [Regulation] applies to companies like yours from [date]. Want a free check of where [company] stands against it, so you know what's left to do?

signal: A vendor announces the end of a product the segment relies on
fresh_window: From the announcement to the end-of-support date
what_it_means: Every user has to migrate. They will compare alternatives anyway.
good_for_sellers_of: Direct alternatives, migration and implementation services
find_with_clay: Company search with technographics.any(product = "[product]") or vendor = "[vendor]".
find_without_clay: The vendor's announcement, then BuiltWith or Wappalyzer, case studies and job posts that name the product.
message_angle: [Product] stops being supported on [date]. Want a side-by-side of what teams like yours are moving to, with the migration effort for each?

signal: A competitor shuts down, is acquired or raises prices
what_it_means: Its customers reconsider whether to stay. Some are already unhappy.
good_for_sellers_of: Direct alternatives
find_with_clay: Company search with technographics.any(vendor = "[competitor]").
find_without_clay: News, the competitor's own customer logos and case studies, G2 and Reddit threads about the change.
message_angle: Saw [competitor] [changed pricing / was acquired]. Want a cost comparison for a team your size before the renewal comes up?

signal: A cost or market shock hits the segment
what_it_means: Budgets tighten and anything that saves money or time gets a hearing. Growth projects get paused.
good_for_sellers_of: Products that cut cost or replace headcount
find_with_clay: Company search by industry and region, then Recent News per company to see who is affected.
find_without_clay: Industry news and association reports.
message_angle: [Shock] usually shows up first in [cost line] for [segment] companies. Want a one-page view of how others in [segment] are handling it?

signal: A trade fair or conference the segment attends
fresh_window: 30 days before to 14 days after the event
what_it_means: People are travelling, meeting suppliers and open to conversations. Exhibitors have spent money and need it to pay off.
good_for_sellers_of: Anyone selling to exhibitors or attendees, especially products for sales and marketing teams
find_with_clay: Paste the exhibitor list into your chat, then a Custom data point per company: 'What is this company presenting at [event]?'
find_without_clay: The exhibitor directory on the event website. Most list company, stand and category.
message_angle: Saw [company] is exhibiting at [event] in [month]. If I put together a list of attendees who match your buyers, would that help your team book meetings before the show?

signal: A job post for the function you serve
fresh_window: 0 to 30 days full, 31 to 90 partial, over 180 expired. Drop it once the role is filled.
what_it_means: They are investing in that area, and soon there will be a new person who needs onboarding, tools and process.
good_for_sellers_of: Tools, training and services for that team
find_with_clay: Company search: jobs.exists(job_title is_similar_to ("[role]") and job_posted_date >= today() - interval 30 days and job_still_open = true). Then verify with a Custom data point that asks for location, date and link.
find_without_clay: Job boards that show dates (in Germany: arbeitnow.com), then the company's own careers page. For companies on Ashby, https://api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/[company] lists every open job with its publish date. Search engines often ignore site: searches on job platforms.
message_angle: Saw you're hiring a [role] for [market]. [What that usually means for them]. If I put together [something the new hire or team can use in week one], would that be useful?

signal: A job post that names a tool or a problem
what_it_means: The description shows their stack, their pain or the project the hire is for. Recruiters write it in plain words.
good_for_sellers_of: Anything the job description names: a tool you replace, a process you fix
find_with_clay: Company search: jobs.exists(job_description contains ("[tool or phrase]") and job_posted_date >= today() - interval 30 days). Add company_size and industry filters: without them this returns the biggest employers first (SAP, Bosch). Read the posting for tools they already use: a post that names a competitor needs a different message.
find_without_clay: Search the phrase on job boards: "[tool]" "[role]" site:jobs.ashbyhq.com, or ask your AI to read the careers page.
message_angle: Your [role] posting mentions [project or tool]. Want a short plan for how teams your size run that project, with the effort for each step?

signal: The first hire in a new function
what_it_means: They are building the function from zero. No tools, no process, and the new person wants quick wins.
good_for_sellers_of: Tools and services a new team needs on day one
find_with_clay: Company search with a job post for the role, then a Custom data point: 'Does this company already employ anyone in [function]? Is this the first hire?'
find_without_clay: LinkedIn people search at the company for the function. If nobody holds it, it's a first hire.
message_angle: Looks like [role] is a new team at [company]. Want the setup we'd use for a new [function] team's first 90 days?

signal: Headcount grew 20% or more in 6 months
what_it_means: Processes that worked at the old size are breaking: onboarding, tooling, reporting, management.
good_for_sellers_of: Ops, HR, onboarding, IT and infrastructure tools
find_with_clay: Company search: employee_growth_6mo >= 1.2 (1.2 means +20%). Or the Headcount Growth data point on your own list.
find_without_clay: The employee count on the company's LinkedIn page over time, or the number of open jobs on its careers page.
message_angle: You've grown about [x]% since [month]. [Process] usually breaks first at that pace. Want a quick check of how yours holds up at twice the size?

signal: A funding round
fresh_window: 0 to 90 days full, 91 to 180 partial, over 365 expired
what_it_means: Money plus a plan to hire and grow. On its own it's weak: everyone writes to funded companies. Combine it with another signal.
good_for_sellers_of: Hiring, scaling and growth tools; recruiting; agencies
find_with_clay: On your own list: the Latest Funding data point. In a search, combine with a job post or headcount growth.
find_without_clay: Crunchbase, Dealroom, Tech.eu, EU-Startups, TechCrunch, or ask your AI: 'Series A rounds in German B2B software announced in the last 60 days'.
message_angle: Saw the [round] in [month]. After a round, [problem you solve] usually comes up within months. Want [a useful asset for it, e.g. the plan we use for a company's first two SDRs]?

signal: Expansion to a new country or a new office
what_it_means: A new market means a new go-to-market: hiring locally, localising, finding first customers, setting up legal and payroll.
good_for_sellers_of: Market entry, localisation, local hiring, payroll and legal, outbound agencies
find_with_clay: Company search: jobs.exists(location contains "[new country]" and job_posted_date >= today() - interval 60 days) plus a headquarters country that is not the new one and a company_size filter, then a Custom data point: 'Has this company announced expansion into [country]? Is it new for them? Link the source.' Without a size filter this returns big multinationals first. Expect many to fail: companies that have been in the country for years, and roles copied across many countries.
find_without_clay: Press releases, job posts in the new country, new office addresses on the website.
message_angle: Saw you're hiring your first people in [country]. Want a list of the first 50 local accounts we'd go after, so the new team has pipeline from day one?

signal: A new product or product line launched
what_it_means: They need demand for something new, fast. The product and marketing teams are under pressure to show traction.
good_for_sellers_of: Demand generation, marketing services, analytics, sales enablement
find_with_clay: The Recent News data point, or a Custom data point: 'What did this company launch in the last 60 days? Link it.'
find_without_clay: The company's changelog, blog, press page, Product Hunt.
message_angle: Saw [product] went live in [month]. Want a list of [segment] companies that look like a fit for it, to test the launch message on?

signal: An acquisition: they bought someone or were bought
what_it_means: Two sets of systems, teams and tools have to become one. Contracts get reviewed.
good_for_sellers_of: Integration, consolidation, data migration, change management
find_with_clay: The Recent News data point, or a Custom data point: 'Has this company acquired or been acquired in the last 90 days?'
find_without_clay: Press releases and business news.
message_angle: Saw [company] brought in [acquired company]. Running two [systems] side by side usually costs more than planned. Want a short plan for merging them, with the effort for each step?

signal: A tool was added to or removed from their stack
what_it_means: They just changed how they work in that area. Adjacent tools are next.
good_for_sellers_of: Tools that integrate with or replace the one that changed
find_with_clay: The Tech Stack data point, or company search with technographics.any(vendor = "[tool]").
find_without_clay: BuiltWith, Wappalyzer, job posts that mention the tool, the company's integration pages.
message_angle: Saw you moved to [tool]. [Adjacent process] usually has to move with it. Want the setup we use to connect the two?

signal: Uses a competitor or a complementary tool
fresh_window: No decay. It is fit, not timing.
what_it_means: They already pay for this category, so they understand the problem. It tells you who, not when.
good_for_sellers_of: Competitors (displacement) and add-ons (integration)
find_with_clay: Company search with technographics.any(vendor = "[tool]"). Tested: technographics.any(vendor = "HubSpot") works.
find_without_clay: BuiltWith or Wappalyzer, the competitor's customer logos and case studies.
message_angle: Combine with a timing signal before writing. Alone: 'Teams on [tool] often [specific gap]. Want to see how [your product] closes it for [their use case]?'

signal: A new executive joined the company (CEO, CRO, CMO, CFO)
what_it_means: New leaders review vendors, set new goals and want early wins. Budgets get reshuffled in the first 90 days.
good_for_sellers_of: Anything in the new leader's area
find_with_clay: Company search: people.exists(is_current = true and job_title is_similar_to ("[title]") and start_date >= today() - interval 3 months). Dates are by month.
find_without_clay: LinkedIn 'started a new position' posts, press releases about the appointment.
message_angle: See the prospect-level version (P1) for the message to the leader.

signal: Layoffs or a restructuring
what_it_means: Fewer people have to do the same work. Cost cuts, but also openness to tools that replace manual work. Be careful with tone.
good_for_sellers_of: Automation and efficiency tools, outsourcing
find_with_clay: The Headcount Growth data point (a negative number), or the Recent News data point.
find_without_clay: News, layoff trackers, LinkedIn posts from affected employees.
message_angle: Avoid mentioning the layoff. Lead with the workload: '[Work] usually lands on fewer people after a reorganisation. Want a short look at how teams cover it with less?'

signal: An award, ranking or certification
what_it_means: They are proud and visible, and often about to grow. A certification such as ISO 27001 also tells you about their process maturity.
good_for_sellers_of: Mostly a reason to talk; a pitch if you sell to certified or fast-growing companies
find_with_clay: A Custom data point: 'Has this company won an award, made a ranking or earned a certification in the last 6 months? Link it.'
find_without_clay: Ranking lists (for example growth rankings in trade press), certification announcements on LinkedIn.
message_angle: Saw [company] made [list]. Growth at that rate usually strains [process]. Want a quick check of how yours holds up at twice the size?

signal: Website traffic jumped or dropped
what_it_means: A jump means a campaign or a launch is working; a drop means something broke (search ranking, a migration, demand).
good_for_sellers_of: SEO, web, conversion and analytics
find_with_clay: The Website Traffic data point on your list.
find_without_clay: Similarweb's free view, or ask your AI to compare with last quarter if it can see traffic data.
message_angle: Traffic to [site] changed a lot since [month]. Want a short breakdown of which pages and sources moved, from public data?

signal: A public tender or request for proposals
what_it_means: They have budget, a scope and a date. This is the most explicit buying signal there is.
good_for_sellers_of: Anyone selling to the public sector or to companies that tender
find_with_clay: Not a Clay search. Find the tender first, then use Clay to find the people at the buying organisation.
find_without_clay: TED (ted.europa.eu) for the EU and national procurement portals. Ask your AI to search them by category code or keyword.
message_angle: Saw the tender for [scope], closing [date]. Want our answer to [one requirement] now, so you can see if we fit before the deadline?

signal: Public complaints about their current vendor
what_it_means: They are unhappy with what they use now. The complaint tells you exactly which pain to lead with.
good_for_sellers_of: Direct alternatives
find_with_clay: A Custom data point: 'Has anyone at this company publicly complained about [vendor] in the last 90 days (G2, Reddit, LinkedIn)? Quote and link it.'
find_without_clay: G2, Capterra, Trustpilot, Reddit, LinkedIn posts. Search "[vendor]" with words like 'switching', 'alternative', 'frustrated'.
message_angle: Quote the pain, not the person: 'Teams moving off [vendor] usually mention [pain]. Want a side-by-side of how [your product] handles it, with the switching effort?'

signal: New in the role (first 90 days)
fresh_window: 0 to 60 days full, 61 to 90 partial, low after that
what_it_means: They are assessing what they inherited, setting a plan and have room to change vendors. The first 90 days are when they decide.
good_for_sellers_of: Anything in their area of responsibility
find_with_clay: Contact search at your target companies: experiences.any(is_current = true and job_title is_similar_to ("[title]") and start_date >= today() - interval 3 months). Or company search with people.exists(...) as in A11.
find_without_clay: LinkedIn Sales Navigator's 'changed jobs in the past 90 days' filter, LinkedIn 'started a new position' posts.
message_angle: You started as [role] in [month]. Most new [role]s review [area] in their first 90 days. Want [a benchmark or audit of their area] to start from?

signal: A past champion changed companies
what_it_means: Someone who used or bought your product before now has a new team, a new budget and a reason to bring tools they trust.
good_for_sellers_of: Anyone with past customers or users
find_with_clay: Contact search with your customers' domains, companyTenure "past", and experiences.any(is_current = true and start_date >= today() - interval 3 months) to see who just started somewhere new.
find_without_clay: LinkedIn: check the profiles of your past users and buyers. Sales Navigator can save them as leads and alert you on job changes.
message_angle: Saw you moved to [company]. Want me to set [product] up there the way you had it at [old company]?

signal: Promoted internally
what_it_means: Bigger scope, new team, and a mandate to show results at the new level.
good_for_sellers_of: Tools and services for the bigger scope
find_with_clay: Contact search at your target companies: experiences.any(is_current = true and job_title is_similar_to ("[new title]") and start_date >= today() - interval 3 months). Then check that the previous role was at the same company.
find_without_clay: LinkedIn profiles: a new title at the same company.
message_angle: Saw you took over [scope]. A bigger scope usually means [new problem]. Want [something useful for it] before it lands on your desk?

signal: Posted about the problem you solve
fresh_window: 0 to 14 days full, 15 to 30 partial, over 60 expired
what_it_means: They are thinking about it right now, in public, in their own words. Use their words.
good_for_sellers_of: Anything that solves the problem they described
find_with_clay: The Find Thought Leadership contact data point, or a Custom contact data point: 'Has this person posted about [topic] in the last 30 days? Quote and link the post.'
find_without_clay: LinkedIn search for posts with the topic, filtered to the last week. Ask your AI to search '[topic]' site:linkedin.com/posts.
message_angle: Your post on [topic] last week, especially [their point], matches what we see at [type of company]. Want the [checklist or approach] we use for exactly that?

signal: Engaged with posts about the problem or a competitor
what_it_means: They are following the topic. Weaker than writing a post, but there are many more of them.
good_for_sellers_of: Anything in that topic area
find_with_clay: Collect the people who liked or commented on a relevant post, then use Clay to find their company and check fit.
find_without_clay: Open the post and read the reactions and comments. Several tools export the people who engaged with a post.
message_angle: Saw you weighed in on [author]'s post about [topic]. Want the [data or example] we have on [the question from the post]?

signal: Spoke at an event, on a podcast or in a webinar
what_it_means: They have a public point of view and like talking about it. Referencing it shows you listened.
good_for_sellers_of: Anything their talk was about
find_with_clay: The Find Thought Leadership contact data point, or a Custom contact data point: 'Has this person spoken at an event or on a podcast in the last 60 days? Link it.'
find_without_clay: Event agendas, podcast directories, YouTube. Ask your AI to search '[name] podcast' or '[name] [event]'.
message_angle: Heard your point on [podcast] about [topic]. We see the same with [related observation]. Want the [data or example] behind it?

signal: Visited your website
what_it_means: They looked at you. Which pages matter: pricing and case studies mean more than one blog post.
good_for_sellers_of: You, the owner of the website
find_with_clay: Send website visitor data into a Clay table (a webhook) and research the company there. The connector doesn't read visitor data.
find_without_clay: Website visitor identification tools (for example RB2B, Dealfront, Snitcher) or your analytics. Be careful with privacy rules in the EU.
message_angle: Never say you saw them on your site. Lead with the topic of the page they read, and offer the most useful thing you have on it.

signal: Engaged with your own content
what_it_means: They know who you are. A cold message becomes a warm one.
good_for_sellers_of: You
find_with_clay: Export the people who engaged with your posts, then use Clay to check fit and find their company.
find_without_clay: Your LinkedIn post analytics and company page followers.
message_angle: Thanks for [reacting to / commenting on] the post on [topic]. Want the [longer version or template] behind it, set up for [company]?

signal: Asked for help in a community or forum
what_it_means: They have the problem right now and they are looking for answers.
good_for_sellers_of: Anything that answers their question
find_with_clay: Not a Clay search. Find the question first, then use Clay to find the person and their company.
find_without_clay: Reddit, Slack and Discord communities, LinkedIn groups, Stack Overflow. Search the problem in their words.
message_angle: Answer the question in the community first. Then: 'Saw your question about [problem]. Want me to [set up / send] [the fix] for your setup?'
